yarn-deadset.meaning: Every beat survives: the perfidiousness joke, the ad in full, Andy's "Why should there be a lady?", Zeke's "indigestion cure instead of the liniment he always got sloshed on", and "it was a kindness to Zeke's memory to give her the job". Nothing invented.
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "shonky business" for graft, "staying back for 'em" for working overtime, "strife with the coppers", "council by-laws and train timetables", "easy on the eye" for praiseworthy to the eye. "co-workers" drops the coeducators pun but is not a wrong sense.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: What Aussie there is sounds natural: "there's dosh in marriage agencies", "We knocked up an ad", "an old mate of mine", "I used to drop in at their place". The narrator's "said I" and "says I" are kept from the original, which suits the period voice.
yarn-deadset.register: A light level 3: the slang is spread thin ("five nippers", "dosh", "flog heaps", "coppers") over a largely original frame such as "Andy gives me one of his looks of calm irritation". No swearing, which is within vulgarity 1. A touch light for the brief.
yarn-deadset.tone: The deadpan con-man comedy stays whole: "'So far, so pernicious,' says I, when we'd finished cooking up the literary masterpiece."
yarn-deadset.flow: Reads smoothly; joins are clean: "That way, and by a careful study of council by-laws and train timetables, I've kept clear of any strife with the coppers".
yarn-deadset.variety: Each term appears once or twice: "shonky", "nippers", "dosh", "knocked up", "flog", "strife", "coppers", "sloshed"; nothing leaned on.
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the original, with its legal mock-jargon kept: "hereditaments and appurtenances set out in the catalogue and writ of errors".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All points survive: the ad, Andy's mermaid line, the rule about the article sold, Zeke's wrong bottle, the visit to Mrs Trotter. "how sneaky women are" renders perfidiousness plainly; nothing is invented.
yarn-dinkum.sense: "off-siders" for partners in a con, "a bit of a swifty" for graft, "lurk" for the scheme, "building society mortgage", "fronting a justice of the peace", "comes sniffing round our agency" all carry the original sense.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian telling it: "Andy gives me one of his looks, calm but fed up", "I used to pop in at their place all the time, and I thought we could get her on board", "wasn't hard on the eye".
yarn-dinkum.register: Right on level 3: steady, natural slang without a pub-yarn frame, and one "bloody" ("a marriage lurk with no bloody marriage in it"), within vulgarity 1.
yarn-dinkum.tone: The comedy and Jeff's mock-legal pomposity come through: "the goods I'm selling have to be real, out where you can see 'em, and handy to produce".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads aloud easily: "See, when you've got enough to spend on advertising--say a roll as big as the little end of a wagon tongue--there's good dosh in marriage agencies."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Mostly varied, but "lurk" is leaned on: "marriage agency lurk", "a lurk like ours", "to work this lurk", "a marriage lurk".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Keeps the shape and the set-pieces; losing "perfidiousness" and "coeducators" softens Jeff's malapropic grandiloquence a little: "I never had much faith in how sneaky women are".

engine.meaning: The original text is kept almost word for word, so the facts survive, but interjections are added that render nothing: "Bloody hell, we had about $6,000", "Bugger me, but where,".
engine.sense: "$3,000 dosh" and "invest dosh with judgment" put slang into the formal ad where it strains, and "she looked a goer" for "feasible" reads as sexually keen when said of a woman.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: swears bolted onto unchanged prose, "reconstructing his bloody mind", "investigate our bloody agency", while US forms stay, "city ordinances and train schedules", "trouble with the police".
engine.register: Largely untranslated apart from "bloke", "nippers", "dosh", "heaps" and "reckoned", yet the swears are dense: "too bloody much", "as bloody big", "Bloody hell", "Bugger me". Within vulgarity 1 but far lighter than level 3 in slang and heavier in swearing.
engine.tone: The scattered swearing roughens a deadpan voice: "'Well,' says Andy, reconstructing his bloody mind".
engine.flow: Clunky joins where swears are dropped in: "Bugger me, but where,' he says, 'could you hope to find a widow".
engine.variety: Leans on "bloody" (six times) and "dosh" (three): "possessing $3,000 dosh", "invest dosh".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original since most of it is the original: "I never had much confidence in the perfidiousness of woman".

unharnessed.meaning: All the points survive; "lady" becomes "sheila" and then "What's a marriage ad got to do with an actual woman?", which keeps the joke. "travelling tent show" is a small colour addition.
unharnessed.sense: Most terms fit ("roped in", "a quid to be made", "given away them ideas", "a good hard squiz at the city by-laws", "front up with"), but "till their feelings or their hairdos get worked up too much" strains, since a hairdo isn't worked up.
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural: "there's a quid to be made in marriage agencies", "I used to drop in at their place a fair bit". "where's the sheila?" is a stock touch, and the ad keeps the US "realizes".
unharnessed.register: Solid level 3, a shade heavier in places ("caper", "sheila", "squiz"); one "pretty bloody well", within vulgarity 1.
unharnessed.tone: Comic tone kept: "in all my dodgy little raids on the letter of the law, whatever's being sold has gotta exist, be seen and be produced".
unharnessed.flow: Reads well, with a few stiff spots: "there was this widow we roped in, me and Andy Tucker, to give us a hand".
unharnessed.variety: Varied overall; "caper" recurs ("marriage agency caper", "a caper like ours", "a marriage caper") and "lurk" also appears.
unharnessed.essence: Recognisably the original with its legal jargon kept: "hereditaments and appurtenances set out in the catalogue and writ of errors".

yarn-troppo.meaning: The story survives, but a frame and claims are invented: "Jeff Peters leans on the bar", "both, mind you, out of the same tent", and "before ya need a New Jersey charter to keep it legal-looking". Asides such as "Beautiful, ay? Pure bait." and "Wrong bottle, poor bugger." are colour.
yarn-troppo.sense: "ya can't trust 'em as far as ya can chuck 'em" says women are untrustworthy in general, muddling Jeff's point that they are too honest for graft; other terms fit ("had a gutful", "wheel out", "fronting a justice of the peace").
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural Aussie voice overall: "Dead calm, but ya can tell he's had a gutful.", "ya can see the cogs turning while he has a rethink". The opener "Now, this one's a ripper." is a stock bolt-on.
yarn-troppo.register: Told as a full pub yarn, with a bar frame, many asides and "bloody good dosh", "the whole flamin' catalogue", "poor bugger": nearer level 5 than the level 3 asked. Vulgarity stays within 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: The humour is kept and the asides suit it: "Wrong bottle, poor bugger."
yarn-troppo.flow: Mostly lively, but the "goes"/"go" and "ya" tics thicken: "'Now listen here,' I go. 'Ya know my rule, Andy."
yarn-troppo.variety: Leans on "I go"/"he goes" for every speech tag and "ya" throughout: "'Jeff,' he goes,", "'Now,' I go,".
yarn-troppo.essence: Still the original's story and set-pieces, but the bar frame and asides shift it towards a different telling: "Now, this one's a ripper. Jeff Peters leans on the bar and goes".

yarn-deadset.quote: As partners or co-workers in even the most innocent line of shonky business
yarn-deadset.original: As partners or coeducators in the most innocent line of graft

yarn-deadset.why: Left as the US form where "building society mortgage" was the easy local swap.

yarn-dinkum.quote: to work this lurk we've got to be able to trot out a real live charming widow
yarn-dinkum.original: to work this scheme we've got to be able to produce bodily a charming widow
yarn-dinkum.why: "lurk" is used four times for the scheme; a reader notices.

yarn-dinkum.quote: I never had much faith in how sneaky women are
yarn-dinkum.original: I never had much confidence in the perfidiousness of woman
yarn-dinkum.why: Plain paraphrase loses Jeff's grand misused word, part of his character.

engine.why: An interjection bolted on where nothing in the original calls for it; reads as pastiche.

engine.quote: possessing $3,000 dosh and owning valuable country property
engine.original: possessing $3,000 cash and owning valuable country property
engine.why: Slang inside a formal newspaper ad breaks the ad's register.

engine.quote: But she looked a goer and praiseworthy to the eye
engine.original: But she looked feasible and praiseworthy to the eye
engine.why: "a goer" said of a woman implies sexual eagerness, not that she was a workable prospect.
"bloody" scattered as filler throughout; one representative quote.

engine.quote: by a careful study of city ordinances and train schedules I have kept out of all trouble with the police
engine.original: by a careful study of city ordinances and train schedules I have kept out of all trouble with the police

unharnessed.quote: till their feelings or their hairdos get worked up too much
unharnessed.original: until they get their emotions or their hair touched up too much
unharnessed.why: "worked up" fits feelings but not hairdos; the zeugma of "touched up" is lost.

unharnessed.quote: as she realizes that the solid virtues are oftenest to be found
unharnessed.original: as she realizes that the solid virtues are oftenest to be found
unharnessed.why: US spelling left in the ad.

unharnessed.original: 'And now,' says I, 'where is the lady.'
unharnessed.why: "sheila" is a dated stock word here.

yarn-troppo.quote: Now, this one's a ripper. Jeff Peters leans on the bar and goes
yarn-troppo.original: "As I have told you before," said Jeff Peters,
yarn-troppo.why: Invents a pub setting and a stock opener the original lacks.

yarn-troppo.quote: ya can't trust 'em as far as ya can chuck 'em
yarn-troppo.original: As partners or coeducators in the most innocent line of graft they are not trustworthy.
yarn-troppo.why: The idiom calls women generally untrustworthy, against the irony that they are too honest to be crooked partners.

yarn-troppo.quote: both, mind you, out of the same tent
yarn-troppo.original: who used to draw soda water and teeth in a tent show
yarn-troppo.why: A new detail rather than a reaction to the original.

yarn-troppo.quote: before ya need a New Jersey charter to keep it legal-looking
yarn-troppo.original: without taking out a New Jersey charter
yarn-troppo.why: Adds an explanation that changes the joke slightly.
"goes" as the speech tag for nearly every line becomes a tic.

summaries.yarn-deadset: A faithful, light retelling with natural slang; a little under-weight for level 3.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Natural, well-pitched level 3 with every point kept; leans on "lurk".
summaries.engine: Mostly the untouched original with swears and "dosh" sprinkled in; pastiche, and "a goer" takes the wrong sense.
summaries.unharnessed: A lively, accurate level 3 with good idiom; a few stiff or stock choices.
summaries.yarn-troppo: A lively full yarn with good idiom, but heavier than the brief, with an invented frame and one muddled idiom.
